title: Anticipatory Token-Window Gating: tenant-aware prefill/decode arbitration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Prototype a tenant-aware gating layer that slices incoming requests into short anticipatory windows and assigns kernel/hardware hints prior to prefill and decode. Goal: reduce tail latency for latency-sensitive tenants while preserving bulk throughput for high-volume tenants through dynamic fairness reservoirs and soft reservations.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prototype that takes incoming requests and classifies them into Window Classes (fast, balanced, bulk) before enqueueing to existing prefill/decode pipeline
Kernel selection hints emitted by gating layer incorporated by runtime router with at least two kernel variants (fast-latency, throughput-quantized)
On the internal benchmark (mixed workload 30% latency-sensitive, 70% bulk) show p95 latency improvement >= 10% for latency-sensitive tenants and throughput loss <= 5% overall
Fairness reservoir prevents starvation: no tenant drops below 80% of baseline throughput for sustained 10-minute burst scenarios
Telemetry added to Console: queue-time by window-class, kernel-selection distribution, and tenant-reservoir utilization
Design doc, unit tests, and a feature flagged rollout path exist; feature can be disabled without restart
updates: 2025-01-15 - Created ticket and initial problem framing. Observed that current prefill/decode allocator treats all requests uniformly, leading to p95 tail spikes when mixed latency and bulk traffic coexist.

2025-01-22 - Spike completed: implemented a lightweight classifier based on request metadata (tenant tier, max_tokens, model_family) and recent per-tenant latency budget. Early results in microbench: window gating can reduce prefill queue time variance by 18% for 'fast' class.

2025-01-29 - Experiment: two kernel variants registered (latency-optimized kernels with lower batchability and throughput-optimized kernels using quantized path). Latency kernels improved p95 by 14% for fast class but decreased throughput by 9% on throughput-only runs.

2025-02-03 - Trade-off decision: introduce soft reservoirs with decay (reservoir credits per tenant) instead of hard reservations to limit throughput regressions while guaranteeing bounded headroom for latency tenants. Chosen params: reservoir window 60s, recharge rate proportional to historical SLA.

2025-02-07 - Integration notes: kernel hints are sent as an annotation on the queued request object rather than separate channel to avoid complex race conditions with autoscaler. Runtime will accept hints but keep final selection based on hardware load signals.

2025-02-10 - Running 12-hour mixed-workload validation in staging. Preliminary metrics: latency-sensitive tenants p95 improved 12%, overall token/sec down 4.6%. Observed a pathological case where many medium-length requests oscillate between classes causing churn; added hysteresis to classifier (30s cooldown).
comments: Ben Gomez (2025-01-23): Good spike work. Need to confirm classifier privacy: avoid leaking tenant usage across classifiers. Consider purely local tenant signals instead of global moving averages.

Marta Varela (2025-01-30): Kernel variants look promising. Please add an experiment measuring NVLink saturation on multi-GPU pods; throughput drops could be due to kernel memory layout, not batching alone.
Connor Liu (2025-02-04): Implemented soft reservoir; still tuning decay. Will add dashboard graphs for per-tenant credit and a heatmap for kernel switching frequency.
Security Review (2025-02-09): No new data surface. Ensure that tenant IDs in telemetry are hashed/obfuscated when surfaced outside SRE team.
notes: Next steps: finalize hysteresis thresholds, run 48-hour soak with multi-tenant synthetic traces, and capture kernel eviction logs to detect oscillation causes.
Consider later extension: allow customers to opt-in with 'latency-target' hint in API headers to avoid tenant-level inference.
If throughput regressions persist, add adaptive demotion: automatically move mid-class traffic to throughput kernels during sustained load to protect global QPS
